name: China economy
summary: China's October CPI rose 0.7% and factory prices 5.7%, fastest in about 4.5 years; no deflation or contagion found
state: China's consumer prices rose 0.7% in the year to October, below forecasts of 0.8%, while producer prices rose 5.7%, the fastest in nearly four and a half years, driven by energy and raw materials (CGTN; New Straits Times, 9 Nov). Q3 growth of 4.5% is near the annual target, though the official manufacturing PMI fell to 49.3 in October. No new property-developer default wave or financial contagion was found as of 11 Nov, so Normal holds.
for_you: Rising Chinese factory-gate prices can feed into the cost of imported goods elsewhere. Firms with supply chains or sales in China are most exposed to any slowdown in demand.
rubric_hit: Growth near target, no deflation or property defaults or contagion found: Normal

sources.title: CGTN — China's October CPI up 0.7%, PPI rises 5.7%
New Straits Times — China's factory-gate inflation at fastest in nearly 4-1/2 years in October

why: China is the world's factory and the biggest marginal buyer of commodities; a hard landing would ripple through every supply chain.
drivers: Property sector, local-government debt, exports and tariffs, deflation, stimulus.

rubric.alert: Hard landing (growth < 3%), financial contagion, or capital controls tightened sharply.
rubric.watch: Deflation, renewed property-developer defaults, or growth clearly below target.
rubric.normal: Growth near official target, stable property sales, no financial contagion.
